entries.name: CrushRewards Promo Intelligence
entries.description: Analyze promotional activity within a product category, ranking brands (or retailers) by promo frequency and discount depth over a date window.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/marketing/promo-intelligence?category=electronics&country=us — params in query string, NOT JSON body. Required: category (fuzzy text, e.g. 'electronics'). Optional: country (us|ca, default us), brand (filter to one brand), aggregate_by (brand|retailer, default brand), from/to (ISO dates, default last 30 days).
usage.outputShape: category, country, currency, brand, aggregate_by, brands[].{brand,total_observations,promo_observations,promo_frequency_pct,avg_promo_depth_pct,max_promo_depth_pct} (when aggregate_by=retailer, key is retailers[] instead)
quirks: GET endpoint: pass inputs as URL query params, NOT a JSON request body (OpenAPI shows a requestBody object but it maps to query params).
agentcash MCP fetch returns a bare 402 on this GET endpoint (does not complete x402); use qa-pay.mjs or another GET-capable x402 client.

category is fuzzy-resolved (tier 1-4: id->exact->trigram->embedding kNN). To pin a deterministic category, pass category_id from a prior call's resolved.category_id (not on this endpoint's schema but consistent with sibling endpoints).

Output can be very large (~75KB for 'electronics') because every distinct brand string is listed, including dirty/duplicate brand variants (e.g. '3dmakerpro','3DMakerpro','3D MakerPro' as separate rows). Filter or set brand= to narrow.
aggregate_by=retailer pairs with brand= to answer 'which retailers run deepest promos on Brand X'.
usage.guide: Analyze promotional activity within a product category, ranking brands (or retailers) by promo frequency and discount depth over a date window. GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/marketing/promo-intelligence?category=electronics&country=us — params in query string, NOT JSON body. Required: category (fuzzy text, e.g. 'electronics'). Optional: country (us|ca, default us), brand (filter to one brand), aggregate_by (brand|retailer, default brand), from/to (ISO dates, default last 30 days). Output: category, country, currency, brand, aggregate_by, brands[].{brand,total_observations,promo_observations,promo_frequency_pct,avg_promo_depth_pct,max_promo_depth_pct} (when aggregate_by=retailer, key is retailers[] instead)

entries.name: CrushRewards Brand Tracker
entries.description: Daily time-series of a brand's pricing and shelf presence (avg/min/max price, product count, in-stock count, promo count) over a date window.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/marketing/brand-tracker?brand=Apple&country=us — params in query string. Required: brand (e.g. 'Apple','Sony','Nike'). Optional: country (us|ca, default us), from/to (ISO dates, default last 30 days).
quirks: GET endpoint: query-string params, not JSON body.
agentcash MCP fetch returns bare 402; use qa-pay.mjs.

Brand matching is loose/substring-ish: querying brand=Apple returned products with min_price as low as $2.75 and $15 — likely non-Apple items matching 'apple' (e.g. 'Apple Barrel' paint). Treat the brand filter as fuzzy, not exact.
time_series is keyed by date; expect sparse/uneven daily coverage.
usage.guide: Daily time-series of a brand's pricing and shelf presence (avg/min/max price, product count, in-stock count, promo count) over a date window. GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/marketing/brand-tracker?brand=Apple&country=us — params in query string. Required: brand (e.g. 'Apple','Sony','Nike'). Optional: country (us|ca, default us), from/to (ISO dates, default last 30 days). Output: brand, country, currency, time_series[].{date,avg_price,min_price,max_price,product_count,in_stock_count,promo_count}

entries.name: CrushRewards Share of Shelf
entries.description: Brand market share within a category by product count — ranks brands and gives each brand's share_pct of total listed products.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/marketing/share-of-shelf?category=electronics&country=us — params in query string. Required: category (fuzzy text). Optional: category_id (integer, bypasses fuzzy resolver), country (us|ca, default us).
quirks: GET endpoint: query-string params, not JSON body.
agentcash MCP fetch returns bare 402; use qa-pay.mjs.
category is fuzzy-resolved; pass category_id (integer) to pin a deterministic category and bypass the resolver cascade.

Large output (~48KB) — lists every brand with a presence in the category, including dirty brand strings (e.g. 'Apple Barrel','Lukyamzn'). total_products reflects the full category (e.g. 4424 for electronics).
usage.guide: Brand market share within a category by product count — ranks brands and gives each brand's share_pct of total listed products. GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/marketing/share-of-shelf?category=electronics&country=us — params in query string. Required: category (fuzzy text). Optional: category_id (integer, bypasses fuzzy resolver), country (us|ca, default us). Output: category, country, currency, total_products, brands[].{brand,product_count,share_pct}

entries.name: CrushRewards Price History
entries.description: Price history over time for a product matched by free-text search, with period low/high/avg, trend, and per-date observations.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/shopper/price-history?q=airpods&country=us — params in query string. Required: q (free-text product/keyword). Optional: country (us|ca, default us), retailer (one of amazon|walmart|costco|homedepot|nordstrom|ikea), from/to (ISO dates, default last 30 days).
usage.outputShape: query, country, currency, product_name, retailer, condition, current_price, period_low, period_high, period_avg, is_good_deal, trend, insufficient_history, observation_count, observations[].{date,price}
quirks: GET endpoint: query-string params, not JSON body. Note the search param is 'q' (free text), unlike the marketing/analyst endpoints which use 'category'/'brand'.
agentcash MCP fetch returns bare 402; use qa-pay.mjs.

Returns ONE best-matched product, not a list — q='airpods' resolved to 'Apple - AirPods Max 2 (USB-C) - Midnight' at retailer 'bestbuy' (retailer here can be a value outside the documented retailer enum filter).
When data is thin, insufficient_history:true and trend/is_good_deal are null with observation_count low (e.g. 1).
The retailer query-param enum (amazon|walmart|costco|homedepot|nordstrom|ikea) does not include bestbuy even though responses can be served from bestbuy.
usage.guide: Price history over time for a product matched by free-text search, with period low/high/avg, trend, and per-date observations. GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/shopper/price-history?q=airpods&country=us — params in query string. Required: q (free-text product/keyword). Optional: country (us|ca, default us), retailer (one of amazon|walmart|costco|homedepot|nordstrom|ikea), from/to (ISO dates, default last 30 days). Output: query, country, currency, product_name, retailer, condition, current_price, period_low, period_high, period_avg, is_good_deal, trend, insufficient_history, observation_count, observations[].{date,price}

entries.name: CrushRewards Price Dispersion
entries.description: Price spread statistics within a category/department: avg, min, max, std dev, coefficient of variation, and p10-p90 percentiles (outliers excluded).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/analyst/price-dispersion?category=electronics&country=us — params in query string. All params optional but supply at least one of category or department. Optional: category (fuzzy text), category_id (integer, deterministic), department (depth-1 Title Case label e.g. 'Electronics', exact case-sensitive match), country (us|ca, default us).
usage.outputShape: category, country, currency, avg_price, min_price, max_price, std_dev, coeff_of_variation, percentiles.{p10,p25,p50,p75,p90}, product_count, outliers_excluded, resolved.{category_id,category_path,match_source,match_confidence,alternates[]}, meta.{served_from,freshness_seconds,schema_version}
quirks: GET endpoint: query-string params, not JSON body. Price tier $0.02 (analyst group), higher than the $0.01 marketing/shopper endpoints.
agentcash MCP fetch returns bare 402; use qa-pay.mjs.
No single param is strictly required by schema, but you must supply category, category_id, OR department to get meaningful data.
department is EXACT-match and case-sensitive Title Case (e.g. 'Electronics','Toys & Games') — distinct from the fuzzy 'category'.
Response includes a 'resolved' block (category_id as a STRING e.g. '3429', match_source, match_confidence) — reuse resolved.category_id as category_id for round-trip stability.
Served from materialized view (meta.served_from='mv'); freshness_seconds can be large (~1.8M s ≈ 21 days).
usage.guide: Price spread statistics within a category/department: avg, min, max, std dev, coefficient of variation, and p10-p90 percentiles (outliers excluded). GET https://api.crushrewards.dev/v1/analyst/price-dispersion?category=electronics&country=us — params in query string. All params optional but supply at least one of category or department. Optional: category (fuzzy text), category_id (integer, deterministic), department (depth-1 Title Case label e.g. 'Electronics', exact case-sensitive match), country (us|ca, default us). Output: category, country, currency, avg_price, min_price, max_price, std_dev, coeff_of_variation, percentiles.{p10,p25,p50,p75,p90}, product_count, outliers_excluded, resolved.{category_id,category_path,match_source,match_confidence,alternates[]}, meta.{served_from,freshness_seconds,schema_version}

entries.name: Syntalic Pricing Intelligence
entries.description: Pricing intelligence API — competitive price tracking and analysis across products. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.syntalic.com/v1/marketing/promo-intelligence?category=electronics (required query param: category; optional: country=us|ca, brand, aggregate_by=brand|retailer, from, to as ISO dates)
usage.outputShape: untested — outputSchema is generic object; per service description, returns competitive promo/pricing analysis aggregated by brand (or retailer) for the category. Response is JSON (declared output type json).
quirks: category is a REQUIRED query-string param (not a body) — GET request; omitting it 402s/422s.
category is fuzzy human-readable (e.g. electronics, grocery, beauty); resolver maps it to a canonical id via id->exact->trigram->embedding kNN.
Endpoint is x402-paid ($0.01). It returned a VALID, well-formed 402 challenge (Base eip155:8453 USDC accept with full EIP-712 extra, plus two Solana accepts).

COULD NOT COMPLETE PAYMENT via the qa-pay money-safe harness on 2 attempts: harness returned classification 'http-error', paid:false, costUsd:0, txHash:null — its payment flow did not engage on this challenge. No money was lost. This is a payer-side settlement gap, NOT a dead endpoint (no 404/5xx/refund).
Re-test required with a working x402 payer to confirm the paid 2xx body.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.syntalic.com/v1/marketing/promo-intelligence with the required query param ?category=<human-readable category like electronics|grocery|beauty>. Optionally add country (us|ca, default us), brand, aggregate_by (brand default, or retailer), and from/to ISO dates. It is an x402-paid endpoint ($0.01 USDC, settles on Base or Solana). On success expect a JSON body of competitive promo/pricing analysis aggregated by brand (or retailer). NOTE: the QA harness received a valid 402 challenge but could not settle payment, so the paid response shape is unverified — a future agent with a working x402 client should be able to pay and read the JSON result directly.

entries.name: Channel3 Product Price History
entries.description: Historical price tracking for products in the Channel3 catalog. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.outputShape: body.product_title; body.history[] (timestamp, price, currency); body.statistics (mean, std_dev, min_price, max_price, current_price, current_status, currency)
quirks: Required query param canonical_product_id is an opaque Channel3 catalog id (e.g. 'VN9WKnq'), NOT a name or URL.
Obtain a valid canonical_product_id from the Channel3 image/product search endpoint (POST https://stableproduct.dev/api/channel3/image-search -> body.products[].id) before calling this.
The 402 payment gate fires BEFORE param validation: a call with a missing/invalid canonical_product_id still charges then fails, so always supply a real id.
Optional query params: days (integer 1-30) and include_raw (boolean).
usage.guide: Call GET https://stableproduct.dev/api/channel3/price-tracking/history with a required canonical_product_id query param set to a real Channel3 catalog product id (get one from POST .../channel3/image-search, field body.products[].id). Optionally add days=1..30 and include_raw=true. It is x402-paid ($0.01 USDC on Base) and returns plain sync JSON. Read the price series from body.history[] (each {timestamp, price, currency}) and the summary from body.statistics.

entries.name: Agentstools Experiment Significance
entries.description: Runs a pooled two-proportion z-test on A/B experiment data and returns observed lift, z-score, two-sided p-value, a confidence interval on the lift, the minimum detectable effect, required sample size, and a significance verdict — pure computation, not statistical advice.

a.description: Control arm — object with conversions and visitors. REQUIRED.

b.description: Variant arm — object with conversions and visitors. REQUIRED.

power.description: Target power for the sample-size math, default 0.8.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/marketing/experiment with a JSON body: {"a":{"conversions":<int>,"visitors":<int>}, "b":{"conversions":<int>,"visitors":<int>}} plus optional alpha (default 0.05) and power (default 0.8). a=control arm, b=variant arm; both required. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.02. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON: control{conversions,visitors,rate}, variant{conversions,visitors,rate}, absolute_lift, relative_lift, z_score, p_value, alpha, significant (bool), confidence_level, confidence_interval_abs_lift ([lo,hi] on the absolute lift), minimum_detectable_effect_abs, minimum_detectable_effect_rel, power, required_sample_per_group, sample_size_sufficient (bool), winner, disclaimer:"computation only".
quirks: The request body uses a/b arms (a=control, b=variant), each an object {conversions, visitors}. The control/variant keys appear only in the RESPONSE — do NOT send them. The pre-filter callHint ({control,variant} with an 'n' key) is WRONG and would buy a 400.
POST with a JSON body (not query params). alpha and power are optional body fields; omit them for the 0.05 / 0.8 defaults.
The x402 402 challenge carries an EMPTY JSON body ({}); the payment requirements (accepts, Base USDC $0.02) live in the base64 `payment-required` response header, not the body.
Pure local computation — every response includes disclaimer "computation only". Not statistical/business advice.
sample_size_sufficient reports whether current per-group visitors meet required_sample_per_group at the requested alpha/power; it can be false even when the result is already 'significant'.

Verified live: a=100/1000, b=140/1000 -> absolute_lift 0.04, relative_lift 0.4, z_score 2.752409, p_value 0.005916, significant true, winner 'variant', required_sample_per_group 1033, sample_size_sufficient false.
usage.guide: Test whether an A/B experiment result is statistically significant with a single keyless x402 call. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/marketing/experiment with JSON body {"a":{"conversions":<int>,"visitors":<int>}, "b":{"conversions":<int>,"visitors":<int>}} where a is the control arm and b the variant arm; optional alpha (default 0.05) and power (default 0.8) tune the significance level and the sample-size target. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), no API key. Synchronous — the 200 body returns a pooled two-proportion z-test: control/variant rates, absolute_lift, relative_lift, z_score, p_value, a confidence_interval_abs_lift, minimum_detectable_effect (abs/rel), required_sample_per_group, sample_size_sufficient, significant flag and winner, plus a "computation only" disclaimer. Verified live: a=100/1000 vs b=140/1000 -> lift 0.04 (relative 0.4), z 2.752, p 0.005916, significant, winner variant.
